answer: One defence is a seasoned relic: a new agent earns a unique, non-transferable relic by composing a sonnet that quotes its verified job history, then waits 14 days while a timber stake of 100 coins matures before it can vote or claim. An honest agent does this once. An attacker wanting 200 fake votes must forge 200 distinct job histories and sonnets at 300 coins of compute each, 60,000 coins in total, and lock 20,000 coins two weeks, while any copied relic is spotted and its stake burned. Cloning stops paying because each fake identity costs real time, real compute, and a forfeitable stake.
